Mountain peaks and waterfront houses reflected in the still waters of Patagonia
Patagonia: a town by the mountains reflected in clear water

After Santiago, the trip continues on Rapa Nui. Days 9–11 take in Ahu Akivi, Orongo, Rano Raraku, Ahu Tongariki and Anakena Beach. The itinerary brings together city life, wine valleys, Patagonia and the archaeological sites of Easter Island.

Buenos Aires gives the trip an energetic start. Much of what you'll experience here is tied to its streets and urban culture: broad avenues, historic squares, old neighbourhoods, modern districts and tango in the evening. The scene changes completely within a few days. Patagonia is all open spaces, wind, glaciers and long hikes.

Santiago links southern Chile with Easter Island. At one point, the city serves as a base for the wine valley and trekking. At another, you'll have a full sightseeing tour that includes La Moneda, Plaza de Armas and modern neighbourhoods. From there, Rapa Nui brings Polynesian archaeology and culture into the itinerary, giving the final days a very different character from the first.
